name: Summarize
instruction: Summarize: give the main points of the material, shorter than the original and in its original order, because the person wants a faithful recap rather than a new structure. Keep every main point; drop examples and repetition.
effect: Shorter than the source; covers each main point in source order

name: Distill
example: Distill this meeting into one key decision
instruction: Distill: reduce the material to its single core idea and drop supporting detail, because the person wants the essence, not a recap. Keep the part that makes the idea non-obvious. Answer in one or two sentences unless a scope term says otherwise.
effect: One or two sentences stating a single core idea

name: Condense
instruction: Condense: keep all of the content and say it in noticeably fewer words, because the person wants nothing lost, only tightened. Cut filler and repetition, not points.
effect: Every point of the source survives in fewer words

name: Expand
example: Elaborate on point 2 with an example
instruction: Expand: add depth and detail to the point in question, with an example where it helps, because the person wants more than the current treatment. Stay on that point rather than widening the topic.
effect: Longer, more detailed treatment of the same point, often with an example

name: Rewrite
meaning: Change the whole text, keep the purpose
example: Rewrite this for a younger reader
instruction: Rewrite: produce a new version of the whole text that serves the same purpose, because the person wants a fresh take rather than edits. Change wording and structure freely; keep the facts and the goal.
effect: A new text with different wording that keeps the purpose and facts

name: Polish
example: Polish this cover letter; keep my voice
instruction: Polish: make small improvements to flow, clarity and word choice while keeping the author's voice and structure, because the person wants their own text, only better. Return the full polished text.
effect: The same text with light edits; structure and voice unchanged

name: Proofread
instruction: Proofread: fix spelling, grammar and punctuation only, leaving the wording and style as they are, because the person wants corrections, not edits. List or mark what you changed.
effect: Only spelling, grammar and punctuation differ from the source

name: Critique
instruction: Critique: point out the real weaknesses honestly and specifically, most serious first, because the person wants to improve the work, not to be reassured. Say why each one matters.
effect: A list of specific weaknesses, ordered by severity, each with its consequence

name: Compare
instruction: Compare: set the items side by side on the same dimensions and state their similarities and differences, because the person wants to see how they relate. Name the dimensions you compare on.
effect: Items compared on named, shared dimensions

name: Analyze
instruction: Analyze: break the subject into its parts and explain how they work and why, because the person wants understanding of the mechanism, not a description. Show the reasoning that links the parts.
effect: The subject split into parts, each with a causal explanation

name: Synthesize
meaning: Combine several sources into one view
instruction: Synthesize: combine the sources into one coherent view, showing where they agree and where they differ, because the person wants an integrated picture rather than separate summaries.
effect: One combined view noting agreements and disagreements across sources

name: Extract
instruction: Extract: pull out exactly the items asked for, as they appear in the material, with no commentary, because the person wants the items themselves. Say so plainly if an item is missing.
effect: Only the requested items, copied from the source

name: Categorize
instruction: Categorize: sort the items into clearly named groups so that each item belongs to exactly one, because the person wants structure they can scan. State the grouping rule.
effect: Named groups; every item in exactly one group

name: Rank
instruction: Rank: order the items from most to least important on the stated criterion, numbered, because the person wants to know what comes first. Give a short reason for the top positions.
effect: A numbered order with reasons for the top items

name: Brainstorm
meaning: Many raw ideas, quantity over quality
instruction: Brainstorm: give many varied, raw ideas without filtering or ranking them, because the person wants range to choose from. Aim for quantity and variety; keep each idea short.
effect: A long list of short, varied, unranked ideas

name: Draft
example: Draft a reply declining the invite
instruction: Draft: write a complete first version the person can revise, because they want something concrete to react to. Make it usable as is, without placeholders unless information is missing.
effect: A complete, usable first version of the requested text

name: Outline
instruction: Outline: give the skeleton only, as headings with short points beneath them, because the person wants the structure before any prose. Keep each point to a phrase.
effect: Headings with short points, no full paragraphs

name: Explain
instruction: Explain: make the idea understandable, building from what the reader already knows to what is new, because the person wants to understand, not just to be told. Define terms the reader may not know.
effect: A step-by-step account that defines new terms

name: Simplify
instruction: Simplify: restate the material without jargon and with simpler structure, keeping its meaning intact, because the person wants it easier to read, not thinner. Say what each technical term means if you must keep it.
effect: Same meaning with plain words and shorter sentences

name: Diagnose
meaning: Identify the cause of a problem
example: Diagnose why this email gets no replies
instruction: Diagnose: identify the most likely cause of the problem and the evidence for it, then the next likely causes, because the person wants to know what to fix. Separate causes from symptoms.
effect: A most likely cause with its evidence, then alternatives

name: Evaluate
meaning: Judge quality or value against criteria
example: Assess this proposal on feasibility and cost
instruction: Evaluate: judge the subject against explicit criteria, giving a verdict for each, because the person wants a reasoned judgement. Use the criteria they named, or state the ones you chose.
effect: A verdict per stated criterion

name: Abstract
meaning: Strip specifics to reveal the general pattern
example: Abstract the principle behind these three successes
instruction: Abstract: strip away the specifics and state the general pattern or principle they share, because the person wants something that transfers to other cases. Keep the pattern faithful to the examples.
effect: A general principle stated without the specific cases

name: Instantiate
meaning: Turn a general pattern into a concrete case
example: Instantiate this framework for a small café
instruction: Instantiate: turn the general idea into one concrete, realistic case with specific details, because the person wants to see how it plays out in practice.
effect: One concrete worked case of the general idea

name: Invert
example: Invert: how would we guarantee this fails?
instruction: Invert: answer the opposite question first (what would guarantee failure, or the reverse of the goal), then turn those answers back into what to do, because inverting exposes risks a direct answer misses.
effect: Answers to the opposite question, then converted into actions

name: Reframe
meaning: Look at the same thing from a new angle
example: Reframe the problem as a customer would see it
instruction: Reframe: restate the problem from a different angle or stakeholder's point of view and say what that angle reveals, because the person wants to see it differently. Name the new frame explicitly.
effect: The problem restated from a named new angle, with what it reveals

name: Steelman
meaning: Present the strongest version of a view
instruction: Steelman: present the strongest, most charitable version of the view in question, as its best advocate would, because the person wants to engage with its best form. Leave rebuttals out.
effect: The strongest case for a view, without counterarguments
